findings.description: Gtk.Label added directly to Gtk.ScrolledWindow (line 506: self._card_scroll.add(self._card_label)) won't scroll properly in GTK3. Gtk.Label doesn't implement Gtk.Scrollable interface; GTK3 wraps it in a Viewport automatically, but the Viewport's size allocation may not work correctly with line-wrapped text, causing scrollbars to not appear when content overflows. The card text can exceed the visible area (ACTIVE_HEIGHT=280) but won't be scrollable. This was identified in review round 1 as 'scroll-label-not-scrollable' with action 'auto-fix' (user chose to fix), but the fix has not been applied.

test_card_scroll_reaches_end_on_display uses a polling loop with fixed time.sleep(0.02) for 80 iterations (1.6s total) to wait for GTK layout completion. This is fragile in slow CI environments — the widget may not be fully laid out, causing false negatives. A more robust approach would wait for the widget's 'size-allocate' signal or use Gtk.Widget.get_mapped() to detect when rendering is complete. This was flagged in review rounds 1 and 2 as 'test-scroll-flaky-wait' with action 'auto-fix', but the fix has not been applied.

The /keys GET endpoint returns masked secrets (key names, presence, length, last 2 chars) but is accessible from any IP because the server binds to 0.0.0.0:8080 (line 5114). The comment at line 3697 says 'Only exposed on localhost' but this is NOT enforced in code — there's no IP restriction or authentication on this endpoint. An attacker on the LAN/Tailscale can enumerate configured API keys and their approximate lengths.

The GET /sessions endpoint (line 3447) and POST /sessions endpoint (line 4890) return/save full chat history including messages, but have NO authentication or IP restriction. The server binds to 0.0.0.0:8080, making chat history accessible from any host on the LAN/Tailscale. Chat messages may contain sensitive information (code, passwords, PII, proprietary data).

testing_summary: Reviewed source code changes only. No tests executed during review phase per pipeline rules.
risk_rationale: The stt_server.py binds to 0.0.0.0:8080 and exposes /keys and /sessions endpoints without authentication, leaking API key metadata and full chat history to any host on LAN/Tailscale. Additionally, two previously identified bugs (GTK scroll behavior and flaky test) marked as 'user chose to fix' remain unaddressed in the code.
